highlights: SCAP barred Liberal Party leader Ichiro Hatoyama from public office on 4 May, and after the Shidehara Cabinet resigned and inter-party talks dragged on, Shigeru Yoshida's coalition cabinet was installed on 22 May.
Arraignment proceedings opened on 3 May before the International Military Tribunal for the Far East against 28 major Japanese war criminals, including Hideki Tojo.
About 1,000,000 citizens joined nationwide May Day rallies, followed by the massive 'Food May Day' demonstration outside Tokyo's Imperial Palace on 19 May.
General MacArthur warned on 20 May against undisciplined physical violence and mass intimidation by disorderly minority groups.
Severe urban food shortages delayed Tokyo-Yokohama rice rationing by 10 to 11 days, prompting SCAP to release 8,705 tons of imported wheat flour in an emergency.
General Orders No. 20 of 3 May discontinued the Civil Intelligence Section as a Special Staff Section and transferred its duties to G-2.
Imperial Ordinance 262 established screening committees to remove militarists and ultranationalists from teaching posts and education administration.
The 26 April census recorded 73,110,995 persons in Japan Proper, adjusted to 74,000,000 for uncounted foreign nationals and transients; 3,789 unions with 1,690,985 members registered.

summary: Summation No. 8 covers non-military activities across occupied Japan during May 1946, documenting a pivotal month dominated by political transition and an acute food crisis. Following the resignation of the Shidehara Cabinet and SCAP's dramatic 4 May directive barring Liberal Party leader Ichiro Hatoyama from public office, protracted inter-party negotiations culminated in the installation of Shigeru Yoshida's coalition cabinet on 22 May. Widespread popular restlessness culminated in historic May Day demonstrations drawing 1,000,000 participants and the massive 'Food May Day' rally in Tokyo, prompting a stern warning from General MacArthur against political violence and an unprecedented radio appeal by the Emperor. Critical staple food shortages in metropolitan centers caused ration delivery delays of up to 11 days, requiring emergency releases of imported American flour. Meanwhile, the International Military Tribunal for the Far East commenced proceedings with the formal arraignment of 28 major war criminals. Other notable developments include the registration of 1.7 million trade unionists, the 26 April census adjusting Japan's population to 74 million, and comprehensive screening regulations to purge militarists from the educational system.
